content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Fredericksburg

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: The PMP requires either a four-year degree plus three years of project-management experience, or a high school diploma plus five years of experience. Review PMI's full eligibility criteria now to confirm you meet the education and documented hours requirement before you enroll.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP course. Over several weeks, active certified practitioners guide you through the PMBOK® Guide, exam domains, and real-world scenarios. Attend sessions on your schedule; all instruction is delivered online, with recorded sessions available for review.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After finishing your 35 contact hours, create your PMI account and submit your official PMP application with proof of education and project experience. Pay the exam registration fee directly to PMI. Expect processing within one to two weeks; PMI will confirm your eligibility status.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice questions, study guides, and coaching—to reinforce domain knowledge. Schedule your exam at a Pearson VUE test center or online. The four-hour, 180-question computer-based exam tests your mastery of project-management principles and practices.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After certification, earn professional development units (PDUs) over a three-year renewal cycle by attending training, teaching, or volunteering on projects. Submit your renewal application and fees to PMI before expiration. Continuing education keeps your credential current and demonstrates your commitment to the profession.
